subject: Civic Education
competence: Investigates public services and understands their historical need, timely importance, and evolution for community development
lesson: Presents views appreciating the importance of public services of the times: The Community Service Case Inquiry: Evaluating Past and Present Impact
unique_learning_outcome: Presents views appreciating the importance of public services of the times.
Investigates information on the beginning and progress of public services.
the_entrance: 5-minute introduction: The teacher writes two contrasting chalkboard prompts: 'Grandfather's journey to the nearest rural dispensary in 1950' versus 'Accessing the local Pradeshiya Sabha water supply and health clinic today.' Facilitating from the center, the teacher challenges the 7 student groups with the launch prompt: 'Imagine walking five miles for a single drop of clean water or medical help—how did our ancestors' struggles shape the robust public utilities we rely on today?' Student teams immediately huddle with their designated Leaders and Scribes, reviewing prior notebook entries on Anuradhapura era medicinal gardens and modern infrastructure to share initial emotional reflections on the hardships overcome by past generations.

lesson_development_steps.teacher_activities: The teacher circulates among the 7 groups, acting as an investigative guide while students examine the historical backdrop of rural electrification and local water boards. The facilitator prompts the Civic Investigators and Secretaries with scaffolding questions: 'What specific administrative hurdles did early village councils face when establishing the first local dispensaries?' The teacher ensures every team member participates in extracting facts from the textbook regarding state and provincial council responsibilities.
lesson_development_steps.student_activities: Civic Investigators and Scribes lead their teams in analyzing chalkboard case prompts regarding the evolution of local Pradeshiya Sabha projects. Group members actively debate the historical difficulties communities experienced before these public services arrived, noting down key milestones from ancient irrigation and hospital setups to modern municipal utility expansions.
lesson_development_steps.learning_teaching_aids: Chalkboard case prompts, Student Notebooks, historical timeline reference cards on Sri Lankan public utilities

lesson_development_steps.teacher_activities: The teacher moves dynamically across the classroom islands, observing group collaboration and moderating discussions as students construct comparative matrices. When a group struggles to connect past hardships with present benefits, the teacher offers probing facilitation: 'How does the absence of profit-making in public services guarantee equal access for low-income families compared to private enterprises?' The teacher verifies that timekeepers are pacing the 15-minute creation of the chart paper deliverables.
lesson_development_steps.student_activities: Working collaboratively on chart paper, the 7 student groups synthesize their findings into a structured case evaluation matrix comparing pre-service hardships with current public service benefits. Timekeepers monitor the 15-minute pacing while Presenters and Secretaries collaborate to draft compelling arguments highlighting the non-profit and equitable nature of modern community services.
lesson_development_steps.learning_teaching_aids: Chart Paper, Colored Markers, Student Notebooks

lesson_development_steps.teacher_activities: The teacher acts as a supportive moderator, inviting selected Spokespersons to share summary highlights of their charts while challenging the class to evaluate the societal impact. The facilitator reinforces key takeaways regarding public service features—such as continuous operation and legal frameworks—ensuring all 35 students remain actively engaged.
lesson_development_steps.student_activities: Spokespersons deliver concise 30-second advocacy pitches summarizing their group's evaluation matrix to the rest of the class. The remaining students act as evaluative peers, nodding in agreement or raising factual inquiries checked by their team's Civic Investigators.
lesson_development_steps.learning_teaching_aids: Chart Paper display sheets, Whiteboard markers

summary: In this 40-minute session, students successfully investigated the historical evolution of Sri Lankan public services from ancient times to the modern era and formulated reasoned appreciation arguments regarding their timely importance and community impact.
assessment_and_feedback_whole_lesson: Formative evaluation is based on group collaboration, the historical accuracy of the chart paper case evaluation matrices, the depth of comparative reasoning between past hardships and present utility benefits, and peer advocacy pitch clarity.
post_activity: 5-minute in-class assignment: Pass-the-Parcel Concept Challenge: The teacher circulates a traditional wooden marker (the parcel) while traditional classroom drumming rhythm plays softly for 30 seconds. When the teacher stops the rhythm, the student holding the marker must immediately draw a Dilemma Card from the teacher's basket—such as 'A rural village petitioning for a new community water tank'—and instantly voice a one-minute reasoned appreciation argument highlighting why this public service is vital for raising local living standards, evaluated directly by class peers.
selected_activity:
Activity: The Community Service Case Inquiry: Evaluating Past and Present Impact
Approach: Student groups examine real-world local scenarios reflecting the establishment and progression of community public utilities like rural electrification, water supply boards, and local dispensaries in Sri Lanka. They investigate the historical difficulties communities faced before these services arrived and formulate reasoned appreciation arguments.
Student task: Civic Investigators review localized case prompts written on the chalkboard regarding the establishment of a local Pradeshiya Sabha water project or post office. The team debates the transformation in citizens' quality of life, drafts evaluation points on chart paper, and prepares an advocacy pitch.
Teacher facilitation: The teacher monitors group discussions across the 7 islands, ensuring equitable role rotation and offering guiding prompts like: 'Compare how your grandparents accessed this service versus how you access it today.'
Expected output: A case evaluation matrix on chart paper comparing pre-service hardships with current public service benefits.
Grouping: 7 teams (7 groups of 5) with assigned roles: Leader / Facilitator, Scribe / Secretary, Timekeeper & Logistics, Spokesperson / Presenter, Civic Investigator / Inquirer.
